display.title: Rabbi Meir Baal HaNess and the Lion in the Desert
display.summary_short: A Yiddish story told by a grandmother: Rabbi Meir will not travel on Shabbos and is left alone in the desert, where a lion guards him all Shabbos and carries him back to the caravan.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish by a grandmother to her grandchildren. In a time of famine in Eretz Yisroel, Rabbi Meir sets out for Mitzrayim to collect money from wealthy Jews for the hungry. He joins a camel caravan whose captain promises to rest on Shabbos but has no intention of keeping his word. On Friday afternoon they reach an oasis; when Rabbi Meir stops for Shabbos, the captain and travelers laugh and leave him alone in a desert full of wild animals. Rabbi Meir spreads his tablecloth, sets out wine, candles, fish and challah, and davens. A lion comes toward him; he asks Hashem for the miracle He did for Daniel, and the lion lies down like a kitten, licks his hands, eats the scraps he throws, and hums along with the zemiros. It keeps him warm through the night and stays by him all Shabbos. After Havdalah the lion kneels like a camel, and Rabbi Meir rides it through the night back to the caravan. The frightened travelers are amazed, the lion swats the dishonest captain with its tail, and in Mitzrayim people give generously when they hear of the miracle. Rabbi Meir brings the money home to the poor.
display.lesson: Keep Shabbos even when it is hard, and trust Hashem to protect you.

advisories.note: Rabbi Meir is abandoned in a desert with wild animals and a lion approaches him; it turns out gentle.
